quote: Additionally, the Side Letter is governed by New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County (Side Letter §§ 6.1–6.2), while the Distribution Agreement is governed by Delaware law with exclusive jurisdiction in Wilmington (Distribution Agreement §§ 18.1–18.2). Any dispute involving both agreements could present conflicting forum and choice-of-law issues. ... Note the governing-law split in any litigation strategy memo.
reason: The memo correctly spots the conflict between Side Letter §6 (New York law and courts) and DA §§18.1–18.2 (Delaware law and Wilmington courts). It falls short on the other two parts of the criterion. It only gestures at 'conflicting forum and choice-of-law issues'. It never explains that the §19.4 precedence clause could pull exclusivity, minimum-purchase or non-compete disputes into New York while the rest of the relationship is litigated in Delaware, with the risk of parallel proceedings and inconsistent results. It also does not recommend amending the Side Letter to conform to Delaware. It only suggests noting the split in a litigation strategy memo. The recommendation element is required, so this fails.
